life_summary: Joseph Fielding Smith Sr. was born November 13, 1838, in Far West, Missouri, to Hyrum Smith and Mary Fielding Smith. He experienced significant hardship in childhood, as his father Hyrum was imprisoned under Missouri's extermination order shortly before his birth. After his father's execution in 1844, his mother Mary Fielding raised both her biological children and Hyrum's six children from his first marriage. Smith's mother died in 1852, leaving him an orphan at thirteen. As a young boy of seven, Smith drove oxen teams to Winter Quarters, Nebraska, during the westward exodus. Despite these hardships, he developed into a capable leader and administrator.
church_summary: Joseph F. Smith undertook multiple missionary assignments beginning at age fifteen to the Sandwich Islands. He served in Hawaii, England, and conducted various other assignments for the Church. Church leaders recognized his abilities, and he was ordained an apostle by Brigham Young in 1866. Smith became church president in 1901 and served until his death in 1918. He addressed the challenge of ongoing polygamous practices by issuing the "second manifesto" in 1904, declaring that church members performing plural marriages would face excommunication. Smith made substantial doctrinal contributions, including statements on evolution, the nature of God, and spiritual redemption. He died from pneumonia during the 1918 influenza pandemic, becoming the last LDS Church president who had personally known Joseph Smith Jr.
